idea-plugin.name: Background ReadAction Freeze Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a background-thread entry point (a `Task.Backgroundable` override, a method annotated `@RequiresBackgroundThread`, an `Application#executeOnPooledThread(...)` task, a task submitted to `AppExecutorUtil`'s pooled executor, or a task passed to `BackgroundTaskUtil#executeOnPooledThread(...)`) that can reach a blocking, non-cancellable read-lock call -- either directly, or transitively through a project method whose own summary already proves it. Java and Kotlin. Every sink is verified against the real `intellij-community` source, and each warning quotes the reason that applies to that exact API: `ReadAction.compute()`/ `run()` are deprecated; `ReadAction.computeBlocking()`/ `runBlocking()` and `runReadActionBlocking {}` are not deprecated, but their own documentation says "Avoid usage in background threads as it will likely cause UI freezes"; `DumbService#runReadActionInSmartMode(...)` runs a blocking read action after smart mode starts; `Application#runReadAction(...)` is not formally deprecated, but its own Javadoc says "Avoid using this method directly in applied/plugins code".

Motivated by JetBrains' own Platform Blog: "Investigating IntelliJ Platform UI Freezes" (Sept 2025) and "UI Freezes and the Dangers of Non-Cancellable Read Actions in Background Threads" (March 2026), which states that "many reports actually show problems in plugins that contain that single erroneous pattern" -- and that detection today is manual, post-mortem thread-dump analysis, not static prevention. This plugin is an attempt at the static side.

Interprocedural: reuses the same real, from-scratch Tarjan's SCC algorithm and whole-project fixed-point summary computation already proven in this catalog's Log Injection Companion and Interprocedural Resource Leak Companion, applied to a simpler reachability lattice.

Validated by hand against real code from `intellij-community` itself (`plugins/hg4idea`): confirmed a real EDT-reachable call correctly NOT flagged (no false positive), and found the `BackgroundTaskUtil#executeOnPooledThread` entry point missing from the original 3-entry list -- added rather than left as a documented gap.

The same rule, applied to IntelliJ's own source, found the blocking read actions reported as IDEA-393501 (`SearchForTestsTask`) and IJPL-257836 (`DependenciesUsagesPanel`).

Stated honestly: Java code is analyzed across the whole project; Kotlin code follows calls only into functions of the same file, matched by name (it works the same in K1 and K2 mode). Kotlin coroutine entry points are out of scope -- JetBrains' own DevKit already reports blocking calls in suspend contexts. `call.resolveMethod()` resolves a virtual Java call to a single candidate (no CHA, no points-to); a project with more than 3,000 analyzable Java methods skips the Java analysis; a hit where the same method also calls `checkCanceled()` is downgraded to a weaker warning, not suppressed -- the write lock can still block. `ReadAction.computeCancellable()` is not reported since 0.3.0: it gives way to a pending write action.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
